accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS 3.NBT.1 and the Year 4 Number and place value requirement (round any number to the nearest 10, 100 or 1000). Every worked value was checked: 37→40, 65→70, 349→300, 367→400, 4,738→5,000, 4,367→4,370/4,400/4,000, 389+512 estimated as 900 against exact 901. The halfway-rounds-up rule is presented as the school convention. Parameterised answers use a−a%u+u×(a%u≥u/2), verified at the range corners (e.g. 25→30, 349→300, 350→400, 4,499→4,000).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented rounding slips: truncating to the first digit (37→30), double rounding (349→350→400, 449→500), looking at the wrong digit, giving the nearest 10 when asked for the nearest 100, and being unsure which way exactly halfway goes. Each appears as a prediction option, a three-ways distractor with its own message, or a tagged challenge answer.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagroundnl is a draggable number line between two multiples showing the distance to each end and a jump arrow to the nearer one, at units of 10, 100 and 1000, plus a three-ways rounding board with the place-value digits and an estimate built from two rounded addends. flagplace shifts digits for ×/÷ 10, flagpvc partitions a four-digit number and flagcmp2d compares with < and >; none rounds. Shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: Distances drive the rule: the learner drags 37 and reads '7 from 30, 3 from 40' before the digit shortcut is stated; at 65 the bars are equal and the halfway-rounds-up rule appears; at 349 the 49-versus-51 bars show why double rounding fails; the three-ways board explains each wrong pick; and the estimate compares 900 with the exact 901.

predictions.evidence: Six predictions, each with a tempting wrong option: '30, because it starts with 3', 'it cannot be rounded' for 65, '400, because 349 rounds to 350 first', '4,000, because it starts with 4', '5,000' or '4,400' for 4,367 to the nearest 1000, and '800, from 300 + 500'. The number line disproves each.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions; wrong answers are tagged first, same, half, twice, unit or up, and each names the slip: keeping only the first digit, not rounding at all, halfway rounds up, rounding in two steps, rounding to the wrong unit, and a deciding digit under 5 rounding down.

readability.evidence: Kid text Flesch-Kincaid grade 1.7 (family target ≤ 5) with worked numbers in each paragraph; adult text grade 5.9 (target ≤ 10) after splitting the mistakes list into short sentences.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passed after replacing a flagged word in the family tip; under 12% overlap with any lesson. Kid paragraphs: nearer multiple, digit rule, 4,367 to 100 and 1000, halfway and one-step rounding. Adult paragraphs: placement, meaning of nearest and the halfway convention, mistakes, what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots of all six steps in both themes: on narrow screens only the end and halfway ticks are labelled so numbers never collide; the distance labels are clamped inside the canvas; the 'halfway' caption is hidden when the marker sits on it after the first pass showed an overlap at 65; the three-ways rows and estimate lines fit 390 px.

accessibility.evidence: Dragging is matched by labelled step buttons (−1/+1 and −10/+10 or −100/+100), labelled answer buttons for each three-ways row and labelled 389 → 300/400 and 512 → 500/600 buttons with aria-pressed. The canvas aria-label states the number, its rounding and both distances after each move. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
